rows.title: Buc-ee’s withdraws application to build 2nd Colorado location
rows.standfirst: The Texas chain withdrew its application to build a supersized travel center in Palmer Lake north of Colorado Springs. The proposal threw the town and neighbors into a bitter battle.

rows.title: Xcel cleared to build huge new series of solar, wind, battery projects. But Colorado’s PUC is wary about costs.
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s largest power provider is rushing to start before federal tax credits expire that could shave up to 50% from building expenses

rows.title: What’s Working: How Denver’s Art Gym went from private passion project to artist co-op
rows.standfirst: It required more than creative thinking. Plus: State Demographer explains Colorado’s population growth, DougCo lands aerospace star tracker, AT&T’s internet purchase, paid-health care internships and more!

rows.title: Some Democrats want to impose new fees on beer, wine and spirits to fund Colorado addiction services
rows.standfirst: The fees would be 26 cents per bottle of spirits, 5 cents per bottle of wine and about 3 cents per six-pack of beer. Small breweries would be exempt.

rows.title: Colorado farmers would need “prescription” to use common pesticide if legislature passes environmental bill
rows.standfirst: Growers worry the bill, backed by the governor, will add bureaucracy and cut yields and profits. Advocacy groups say neonicotinoids are being used as an insurance policy.

rows.title: Why your Colorado property tax bill still increased this year
rows.standfirst: The state had granted temporary tax discounts in recent years, but they are expiring. At the same time, tax rates paid to schools are also effectively increasing.

rows.title: Legislature rejects attempt to let Colorado communities increase taxes on often-vacant homes
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1036, geared toward addressing the housing shortage in resort communities, would have let the revenue generated by the new taxes pay for affordable housing projects

rows.title: Workers at JBS plant in Greeley prepare to launch nation’s first meatpacker strike in decades
rows.standfirst: The union is protesting unsafe working conditions and an expired contract, while also supporting Haitian immigrants who could lose TPS status

rows.title: Are Flock and Palantir both owned by billionaire Peter Thiel?
rows.standfirst: No. While Peter Thiel cofounded Palantir, he has never been on Flock’s board and did not help start the company.

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver prices grew faster than US in January
rows.standfirst: Coloradans may have adjusted to higher prices but they’re not by cutting back on sports or outdoor activities, says Red Rocks Credit Union poll. Plus: Colorado’s global trade, free tax help day and more!

rows.title: Colorado childcare centers can hardly afford to stay open, and many families can’t afford to enroll without government help
rows.standfirst: The state’s childcare system was barely staying afloat even before the latest upheaval in federal support

rows.title: Is rent getting cheaper in major Colorado cities?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Median rents in large Front Range cities fell across the board in late 2025 compared with the same period a year earlier, reports show.

rows.title: Palantir departs Denver, moves headquarters to Miami
rows.standfirst: Valued at $300B, Palantir was the largest publicly traded company in Colorado. CEO Alex Karp recently bought a monastery in Old Snowmass.

rows.title: Federal proposal limiting foreign scientists at Boulder lab disrupts Colorado’s quantum industry
rows.standfirst: A proposed update to a federal security policy on government-funded research could shut out non-US associates at NIST, the federal lab, after March 31.

rows.title: Heat pump installations in Colorado more than doubled in 2025 as rebates expired and contractors mastered service
rows.standfirst: Xcel Energy and Tri-State primed the heat pump boom, training hundreds of private installers to help encourage the shift to clean heating and cooling

rows.title: Parts of beloved El Rancho building will move, “preserving the essence,” as huge gas station takes its place
rows.standfirst: Evergreen, county officials praise a compromise that moves elements of the building to a new public arts pavilion, but a planned QuikTrip at El Rancho exit remains controversial

rows.title: Food banks in Colorado mountain towns are struggling to keep residents fed amid low snow year
rows.standfirst: Record traffic from underworked, overstressed residents pushes food banks to the brink. “Really hoping that our communities survive this.”

rows.title: Colorado companies look at implications after US Supreme Court rules against Trump’s tariffs
rows.standfirst: Colorado small businesses scrambled last spring to adjust orders, reroute manufacturing and find cash to pay the higher tariffs

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado union membership fell 22% last year. Labor unions say they didn’t see a decline.
rows.standfirst: Colorado AFL-CIO said drop may be linked to end to collective bargaining of federal workers. Plus: Colorado salaries, flat rents in 2026, more!

rows.title: The sale of Fort Collins’ Old Firehouse Books reveals how intangibles influence the book business
rows.standfirst: When Susie Wilmer stepped back from the independent bookstore she nurtured for 25 years, she — like others in her position — couldn’t sell to just anybody

rows.title: Nederland closer to removing Caribou Village fire debris, but the future remains uncertain
rows.standfirst: Site stabilization that concluded Friday will allow safe access to parts of the demolished building where asbestos could be lurking

rows.title: Proposed tax breaks for data centers would increase taxes for poor Coloradans, analysts say
rows.standfirst: Sponsors of industry-backed data center bill say they are amending it in ways that will change the fiscal projections

rows.title: Solar power taking only tiny fraction of Colorado farmland despite fears, industry study shows
rows.standfirst: Some local officials worry solar could take a big bite out of agricultural land. So far, it has amounted to less than 1%, trade group says.

rows.title: Denver proposes data center cutoff as ire grows against tax breaks, environmental cost
rows.standfirst: Mayor and council cooperating on building moratorium, while state Legislature debates expense of tax breaks

rows.title: AI chatbots operating in Colorado would have to take steps to protect kids, prevent suicides under bipartisan bill
rows.standfirst: The measure represents the legislature’s latest attempt to address artificial intelligence as the technology becomes increasingly prevalent

rows.title: How these Colorado businesses changed course during the chaotic 2025 tariff wars
rows.standfirst: One company moved some manufacturing to the US from China, while another is moving it to Denmark. Both blame the tariffs.

rows.title: Greeley voters reject project that would have built a new arena for the Colorado Eagles
rows.standfirst: A voter-backed measure will repeal the zoning permit for a proposed city-owned, $1 billion entertainment district in West Greeley.

rows.title: Federal judge clears way for luxury Berlaimont developers to build their access road near Edwards through Forest Service land
rows.standfirst: The ruling aligns with nearly two dozen others who challenged whether 1980 legislation in Alaska applies in the rest of the country. Environmental groups who sued say they have additional claims still pending.

rows.title: Award-winning Vietnamese restaurant in Denver finds its James Beard future on ice
rows.standfirst: A monthslong behind-the-scenes battle goes public when sắp sửa chef Ni Nguyen tells his side. Meanwhile, the prestigious restaurant awards organization stays silent.

rows.title: Xcel posts nearly $1 billion operating profit from Colorado as the utility seeks rate increases for gas, electric customers
rows.standfirst: Settlements related to the Marshall fire trimmed the bottom line to $678 million, the lowest in four years

rows.title: What’s Working: How an Estes Park workforce housing program is rewarding renters
rows.standfirst: Cash back, property equity and an effort to close the workforce housing gap. Plus: Report shares data behind Denver’s struggling restaurant scene, why a Fort Collins brewery is getting a billboard, more!
